input.question: If matter attracts matter (gravity), does anti-matter repel matter (anti-matter)?
input.ground_truth: Gravity is a response to mass, it doesn't care what kind of matter has the mass. Both matter and antimatter have mass, and so will attract each other. A normal hydrogen atom would be gravitationally attracted to an anti-hydrogen in exactly the same way that it would be attracted to a normal hydrogen. Dark Energy is unrelated to this concept -- it refers to the accelerated expansion of space itself in the universe.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If matter attracts matter (gravity), does anti-matter repel matter (anti-matter)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have some special blocks called "matter blocks." They like to stick together because of gravity, kind of like how magnets can stick together.

Now, imagine there are also "anti-matter blocks." These are like the opposite of the matter blocks. When a matter block meets an anti-matter block, instead of sticking together, they push each other away very, very strongly! They don’t like to be near each other at all. 

So, yes! Anti-matter blocks *repel* (push away) matter blocks. They don’t want to be friends—they want to stay far apart!
